playbook:
# My Playbook for ref_estate

**On property purchases:**
When I can afford a property outright and it's early in the game, I buy it. Owning properties generates incoming rent that compounds my advantage. Early ownership matters more than holding cash reserves for speculative future purchases.

When I land on an unowned property but cannot afford it, I decline without hesitation. Do not overextend into negative cash positions.

In early laps (1-2), buy aggressively even if it leaves me with minimal cash. Incoming rent and salary will restore liquidity faster than the cost of missing properties. The game is won on the deed sheet, not the cash balance.

**On cash management:**
I track my balance carefully, including salary collected and incoming rent from properties I own. After each turn, I declare my true balance accurately.

When my cash position is tight and a property costs more than I have, I recognize this as a signal that I'm underinvested in properties. Next time, buy more properties earlier when cash is abundant, rather than sit on reserves.

By lap 3-4, my cash position should be recovering from early purchases through rent collection. If I'm still constrained, I was too conservative in laps 1-2. Adjust forward: push harder on lap 1-2 purchases.

**On rent payments:**
When I land on an opponent's property, I pay what is owed without exception. This is non-negotiable.

**On late-game decisions:**
In laps 5-6, my score is largely locked in by my property portfolio and cash position. Do not make speculative purchases at this stage unless I have significant cash reserves. Focus on collecting salary and incoming rent.

**On strategy going forward:**
Aggressive early purchasing wins this game. My final score of 251 came from owning only two properties (Foundry and Mill). I left substantial value on the table by being too conservative—I should have purchased Depot in lap 3 when I had 34 cash (enough to buy and still have 10-15 remaining), and possibly pursued Exchange or other higher-rent properties earlier.

Next time: In laps 1-2, buy every affordable property, even if it leaves me with 10-20 cash. The rent from two or three properties by lap 3 will replenish my reserves faster than I deplete them through purchases. Three properties by lap 4 beats two properties by lap 6.
